title: Receipts/Req2283ClosedGenericStructFromReferencedAssemblyTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (4/4), passes on head (4/4); refutes 1 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-1

refutes.claim: The requirement names three unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites, at reporter lines 735, 1009 and 1101. The diff fixes only two of them: base lines ~985 and ~1077, which match 1009 and 1101 at a constant -24 offset. No hunk touches the site matching reporter line 735 (about base line 711). The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper only filters diagnostics after they are created, and the location is computed before that. So if `[0]` is still indexed there and that path runs for `Item<int>`, the generator and analyzer would still throw `IndexOutOfRangeException`.

title: Receipts/InheritedMetadataMemberNeedsKeyTests.cs: edge-case test passes on head (1 tests): no defect shown; refutes 1 lens claim(s): logic-edge-1

refutes.claim: When a `[MessagePackObject]` type declared in source inherits an unkeyed public field from a base class in a referenced assembly, MsgPack004 is now silently dropped. The guard at the changed line checks only `formattedType.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.IsEmpty`, and `formattedType` here is the source type, so the diagnostic is still built. But `item` (the inherited field) comes from metadata, so `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()` gives a null location, i.e. `Location.None`. The new wrapper `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` (line 239, body at 1446) then throws the diagnostic away. The user's own source type gets no error for a public member that has neither `[Key]` nor `[IgnoreMember]` (L3), and nothing tells them the member is mishandled. Base crashed here (AD0001); head swaps the crash for a silent miss instead of reporting at a fallback location such as the derived type's identifier. The `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull` path via `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` has the same gap for inherited metadata properties.
